story:
The previous seasons of elk hunting had taught me a great deal about calling. My dad was excellent with a cow call, and together we had enjoyed some close encounters. The year before had shown us how the elk used this country—where they moved, how they traveled, and where they preferred to bed. I learned that if you could slip in close without the animals knowing you were there, you could often convince them you belonged.

Every so often we even managed to get a bull to answer from his bed.

That morning one particular bull had been talking steadily but refused to come in. We let him and his cows bed down, then eased in close. We began with soft cow calls and got him to answer. Then we hit him with a bugle, imitating a rival bull trying to slip in on his cows. He came in screaming, charging to defend his herd, and stopped at twenty yards. I made a solid shot, and he went only thirty yards.First paragraph of the story.
